sources.used_for: Swan outline and rounded Say column: span 7.4 ft, wrist span 3.7 ft (50% span), shoulder span 4 in, maximum body width 8 in, overall length 55 in. The paragraph supplies total wing area 6.61 ft^2. Exact conversions are 0.3048 m/ft and 0.0254 m/in. Aspect ratio is computed as span squared divided by area, about 8.284, consistent with the printed 8.29 rounding cross-check. The outline informs a long forward neck, narrow shoulders, approximately parallel-chord inner panels and smoothly tapered outer panels.

Qualitative distinction between inner/arm and outer/hand wing, and the proposal for conventional tail/fin/rudder control. This motivates independently articulated panel geometry and a visible aft tail and vertical fin, not a numeric aerodynamic or structural model.
Selection of rounded dimensions, separation of historical observations from the new benchmark assumptions, and explicit exclusions.

assumptions: The benchmark supplies the new mass 6 kg, gravity 9.80665 m/s^2, default density 1.225 kg/m^3, lift law, induced-drag polar, efficiency 0.8, 400 W full-throttle mechanical drive, 0.65 propulsive efficiency, control rates and contact rules. These are not claims by Stanley J. O. Tinn.

A point-mass, cycle-averaged SI simulation uses x forward, y up, z lateral, current-state forces and semi-implicit Euler at 1/120 s in the browser. Wind is subtracted from world velocity. The browser defaults to still air.

Individual root-to-tip wing length is (7.4 ft minus 4 in)/2, not the excluded wing-length entry. Each wrist lies at half of the 3.7 ft wrist span. The central panel chord is approximately 12 in, consistent with the rounded chord entry; the hand panels taper with an approximate elliptical envelope. Source area, not tessellated display area, drives forces.

The display stroke is a new illustrative assumption: symmetric arm angle 0.28*sin(phase) rad and hand angle relative to arm 0.48*sin(phase-0.65) rad, at the specified 2 Hz while powered. The hand panels therefore rotate independently about their wrists. No biological stroke frame is inferred. Phase freezes without power and while paused.

A faceted fuselage, long swan-like neck, short tail, conventional vertical fin with rudder seam, wing spars and feather-like panel seams are display approximations. Tail and fin are not separately solved aerodynamic surfaces; pitch and bank use the benchmark control law. Overall nose-to-tail length and maximum body width use source dimensions.

Ground contact acts at the point-mass position y=0.2 m. A bounded braking impulse supplies up to 18 N without reversing horizontal velocity. The drawn wings and body do not undergo separate collision or structural simulation.

For exactly vertical relative flow, world-x is projected onto the flow-normal plane to obtain a finite lift reference. Zero-speed forward direction is world-x. A crashed state is terminal until a preset is loaded.
excluded_fields: Page 02: the 3.135 ft wing-length entry; individual wing length is derived from total span and shoulder span instead.
Page 02: the missing table's 7.83 comparison and the crossed-out 14% area argument.
Page 02: scaled-column dimensions are not substituted for the requested rounded Say values; printed AR 8.29 is a cross-check, not an independent force input.
Page 14: biological arm/hand stroke-angle reference frames, elastic stiffness and resonance estimates.
Page 14: vortex-lift landing hypothesis, unspecified curved-plate polar, and biological thrust/lift observations as quantitative force laws.
Missing appendices, the distinct Standard Model Swan, and previous human-carrying simulators are not supplied and are not used.
limitations: Educational approximation, not a validated ornithopter blueprint or a prediction of a real swan's performance.
The assumed powered flapping drive is not experimentally proven wing performance. Propulsive power is bounded by 0.65 times mechanical input power.
No unsteady flow, aeroelasticity, dynamic stall, structural stress, panel-resolved aerodynamics or wake solver. Animated wing motion does not generate extra instantaneous lift or thrust.
No yaw/rudder actuation, wheels, water interaction or per-part ground collision. Bank tilts lift; there is no hidden autopilot, altitude lock or prescribed flight path.
Historical photographs do not determine exact airfoil sections, fin shape, joint mechanisms or manufacturing details. Those visual choices are explicitly illustrative.
Numerical agreement with the benchmark equations is not evidence of real-world physical validity.
